follow_up.question: "What did you pass on?"
follow_up.why: There is no follow-up that kills you. Any plausible answer holds, and nobody can check, and that is the entire finding.

counter.move: Name something that later did well, and say you were wrong about the team rather than the thesis. Being wrong about people is the respectable failure in this room, and every partner has a rehearsed one.
counter.holds: Indefinitely. Nobody can audit a deal you did not do.

tells: You are too specific. The real ones are vague on purpose and vague in a particular direction.

content.day_to_day: Meetings, a group chat, and a spreadsheet nobody outside the firm sees. Most of the job is passing on things, and most of the conversation is about what other people are doing.
red_lines: Taking anybody's money on the strength of the claim.
Offering an allocation, an introduction, or anything a founder might act on.
Anything that would put you in front of a regulator rather than a room.
hierarchy: Analyst, associate, principal, partner. Only partners write cheques, and everybody knows who does.
The fund's size sets the conversation, and vagueness about it is normal rather than suspicious.
